current.Title: VIC-II + SID VICE-fidelity audit: divergences from viciisc/reSID
Description: [01] SID scope: reSID at native/vice/vice/src/resid is the specification. Live impl is src/ViceSharp.Chips/Audio/Sid6581.cs (+Sid8580,Sid8580D). Sid/Mos6581.cs and SidOscillator.cs are dead/unused.

[02] SID envelope FAITHFUL: rate_counter_period, sustain_level, exponential thresholds, the 0x8000 ADSR delay bug, the three pipelines, and register-write logic are bit-exact vs reSID envelope. The only faithful SID subsystem.

[03] SID envelope minor divergences: power-up counter seeded 0x00 vs reSID 0xaa (first-attack length + idle ENV3); envelope OUTPUT applied linearly with no model_dac; dead AttackRates/DecayReleaseRates tables hold wrong values; ProcessEnvelope comment wrongly says batched/SAMPLE_FAST.
[04] SID waveform combined: naive bitwise AND; reSID uses measured ROM tables (wave6581_*, wave8580_*) NOT ported. All combined waveforms wrong. Sid6581.cs:202-206 vs wave.h:458-498. CONFIRMED.
[05] SID waveform pulse: duty inverted. Managed HIGH when phase<pw; reSID HIGH when acc>>12>=pw. Exact opposites (pw=0: managed silent, reSID constant-high). Sid6581.cs:169 vs wave.h:243. CONFIRMED.

[06] SID waveform ring-mod: managed XORs whole triangle output on modulator MSB; reSID substitutes the triangle fold MSB and gates on sawtooth deselected. Wrong operation, polarity, gating. CONFIRMED.
[07] SID waveform hard-sync: managed resets on falling MSB edge; reSID resets on rising MSB edge (msb_rising). Opposite edge; missing same-cycle sync-source special case. CONFIRMED.

[08] SID noise LFSR: single register shared across all 3 voices (should be per-voice); runs only when noise selected (should free-run); no 2-cycle shift pipeline; no combined-waveform LFSR lock-up. CONFIRMED.
[09] SID TEST bit: instant LFSR reseed to 0x7FFFFF vs reSID ~35000-cycle fade; pulse not forced high during test; no falling-edge single clock. CONFIRMED.
[10] SID OSC3 ($D41B): returns raw accumulator phase for all non-sawtooth waveforms; should return selected waveform output. This is why the sawtooth-only parity test passes. CONFIRMED.
[11] SID resolution: 8-bit waveform path throughout vs reSID 12-bit + model_dac R-2R DAC. 4 bits + DAC nonlinearity lost. CONFIRMED.

[12] SID filter: generic Chamberlin state-variable filter. NONE of reSID op-amp spline/opamp_rev, cutoff-DAC/build_dac, EKV/VCR integrator, or resonance/mixer/gain tables exist. Structural, cannot be tuned to match. Sid6581.cs:282-365. CONFIRMED.
[13] SID filter clocking: integrated once per 44.1kHz output sample, not per phi2 cycle. Not cycle-deterministic. CONFIRMED.
[14] SID filter variants: 6581 and 8580 are the same SVF with tweaked coefficients, not reSID two separate models. Sid8580D is a memoryless gain-scaler stub. CONFIRMED.
[15] SID external filter (extfilt): absent entirely. C64 output 16kHz low-pass + 16Hz DC-blocking high-pass missing. CONFIRMED.
[16] SID cutoff mapping: hand-authored piecewise-linear Hz table vs reSID f0_dac R-2R nonlinearity; 6581 cutoff kinks absent. CONFIRMED.
[17] SID resonance: invented linear 1/(1+res/4) vs reSID inverted-res nonlinear table-driven gain; res=15 near-self-oscillation not modeled. CONFIRMED.
[18] SID volume/mixer: linear scalar vs reSID nonlinear gain[vol] op-amp DAC; digi is a fabricated DC constant not the mixer nonlinearity. CONFIRMED.
[19] SID voice-3 disconnect ($D418 bit7 / 3OFF): dropped (control masked 0x70). V3-mute is a no-op; voice 3 stays audible. Audible bug. CONFIRMED.
[20] SID output resampling: bare point-decimation (one cycle per ~22), no band-limiting FIR; cruder than reSID SAMPLE_FAST. CONFIRMED.
[21] SID databus/TTL: no bus_value fade (6581 0x1d00 / 8580 0xa2000); write-only registers read stored byte forever; SID-detect wrong. CONFIRMED.
[22] SID POT ($D419/$D41A): returns 0x00 vs reSID 0xFF; no paddle timing. CONFIRMED.
[23] SID 8580 write pipeline (1-cycle delay) not modeled; amplify scaleFactor (6581=3,8580=5) absent so relative loudness wrong. CONFIRMED.

[24] SID tests give false confidence: SidEngineParityTests is sawtooth-OSC3 only; SidCombinedWaveformTests asserts the naive-AND. Green SID tests validate the approximation. Must be replaced with reSID-derived exact-equality tests.
[25] VIC-II scope: viciisc at native/vice/vice/src/viciisc is the spec. Impl is VicIi/Mos6569.cs + VideoRenderer.cs + Core/C64MemoryMap.cs.

[26] VIC-II FAITHFUL: per-mode colour math (colors[]), register I/O masks + live read-backs, IRQ latch/enable + 9-bit raster compare, invalid-mode-to-black + priority bit, VC@13/RC@57 timing, g-fetch address math, refresh, sprite-DMA turn-on cycles, reset state.

[27] VIC-II render architecture (HEADLINE): whole-line geometric reconstruction (RenderRasterLine re-reads video RAM at line-end) vs VICE per-cycle 8px shift-register draw. Every mid-line change except $D020/$D021 lost; g-data re-read at render time so mid-line $D018 lost. CONFIRMED.

[28] VIC-II colour pipeline: no cregs one-pixel delay; no color_latency/grey-dot; $D022-$D02E mid-line changes lost; $D020/$D021 replay quantised to 8px boundaries with tuned FirstVisibleRasterX=12 vs DBUF_OFFSET geometry. CONFIRMED.
[29] VIC-II fine scroll: $D016 XSCROLL never applied to graphics pixels. CONFIRMED.
[30] VIC-II mode split: display mode/columns/colour sampled once per line; mid-line ECM/BMM/MCM/CSEL changes lost. CONFIRMED.
[31] VIC-II matrix addressing: screen row derived geometrically from raster, not the VC counter; diverges under vc/vcbase manipulation (FLD, DEN). CONFIRMED.
[32] VIC-II 38-column stride: reads screen[row*38+col] instead of row*40+col in 38-col mode (Mos6569.cs:1237). Wrong char/colour addresses. Concrete bug. CONFIRMED.
[33] VIC-II VC/VCBASE not reset at frame start (only Reset()); after frame 1 loads stale value. Breaks per-cycle lockstep. CONFIRMED.
[34] VIC-II bad-line off-by-one: allow_bad_lines cleared at >0xF8 not ==0xF7; one extra bad line at 0xF7 with YSCROLL==7. CONFIRMED.
[35] VIC-II DEN re-check: sampled once at line 0x30 start, not per-cycle; mid-line DEN enable on 0x30 missed. CONFIRMED.

[36] VIC-II c-access: one cycle late + collapsed with g-access (not pipelined); first 3 matrix slots hardcoded 0xFF/CPU-bus vs the prefetch_cycles counter, 3 wrong leading columns in lockstep buffer. CONFIRMED.
[37] VIC-II reg11 delay: BMM/ECM use current $D011 not last-cycle-delayed; 6569 char-ROM address-latch absent. CONFIRMED.
[38] VIC-II sprites rendering: whole-line geometric recompute from memory vs VICE per-pixel sbuf shift-register with xpos trigger + expansion/mc flip-flops. CONFIRMED.

[39] VIC-II sprites DMA: no mc/mcbase/exp_flop, no mcbase==63 stop, no display-bit latch; DMA a fixed 21/42-line window by line-counting; pointer/data read live at render time. Sprite crunch and mid-line $D017 not reproduced. CONFIRMED.
[40] VIC-II sprites collisions: once-per-line geometric with a single IRQ latch point, from a separate pass not the drawn pixels; per-pixel timing and border/off-screen collisions differ. CONFIRMED.
[41] VIC-II sprites multi-sprite priority: managed substitutes a lower-priority in-front sprite where VICE shows background (loop+continue vs winner-first). Behavioral bug. CONFIRMED.

[42] VIC-II border rendering: per-cycle main/vertical flip-flops feed only per-line boolean snapshots; border extent (geometry) + border colour ($D020 log) are two bolted approximations vs VICE single per-cycle draw_border8; no CSEL pixel-7 edge. CONFIRMED.
[43] VIC-II border-FF cycle base: LeftBorderCheckCycle 17/18 and RightBorderCheckCycle 56/57 are +1 vs VICE 0-based 16/17/55/56, inconsistent with correct VC@13/RC@57. CONFIRMED.
[44] VIC-II raster IRQ timing: fires one cycle late (RasterX==1 vs raster_cycle==0) for all lines except line 0. CONFIRMED.
[45] VIC-II raster IRQ re-arm: $D011/$D012 writes re-arm unconditionally (no unchanged-value guard, no raster_irq_triggered latch); handler can double-fire on same line. CONFIRMED.
[46] VIC-II collision clear: $D01E/$D01F cleared immediately on read vs VICE deferred to next cycle; no collision-enable gate. CONFIRMED (low).
[47] VIC-II light pen ($D013/$D014): X latch RasterX>>1 (0..31) vs VICE cycle_get_xpos/2 + x_extra_bits (~12..250); no delay, guards, frame retrigger, or old-6569R1 mode. CONFIRMED.

[04] SID waveform combined: naive bitwise AND; reSID uses measured ROM tables (wave6581_*, wave8580_*) NOT ported. All combined waveforms wrong. Sid6581.cs:202-206 vs wave.h:458-498. CONFIRMED.
[05] SID waveform pulse: duty inverted. Managed HIGH when phase<pw; reSID HIGH when acc>>12>=pw. Exact opposites (pw=0: managed silent, reSID constant-high). Sid6581.cs:169 vs wave.h:243. CONFIRMED.

[06] SID waveform ring-mod: managed XORs whole triangle output on modulator MSB; reSID substitutes the triangle fold MSB and gates on sawtooth deselected. Wrong operation, polarity, gating. CONFIRMED.
[07] SID waveform hard-sync: managed resets on falling MSB edge; reSID resets on rising MSB edge (msb_rising). Opposite edge; missing same-cycle sync-source special case. CONFIRMED.

[08] SID noise LFSR: single register shared across all 3 voices (should be per-voice); runs only when noise selected (should free-run); no 2-cycle shift pipeline; no combined-waveform LFSR lock-up. CONFIRMED.
[09] SID TEST bit: instant LFSR reseed to 0x7FFFFF vs reSID ~35000-cycle fade; pulse not forced high during test; no falling-edge single clock. CONFIRMED.
[10] SID OSC3 ($D41B): returns raw accumulator phase for all non-sawtooth waveforms; should return selected waveform output. This is why the sawtooth-only parity test passes. CONFIRMED.
[11] SID resolution: 8-bit waveform path throughout vs reSID 12-bit + model_dac R-2R DAC. 4 bits + DAC nonlinearity lost. CONFIRMED.

[12] SID filter: generic Chamberlin state-variable filter. NONE of reSID op-amp spline/opamp_rev, cutoff-DAC/build_dac, EKV/VCR integrator, or resonance/mixer/gain tables exist. Structural, cannot be tuned to match. Sid6581.cs:282-365. CONFIRMED.
[13] SID filter clocking: integrated once per 44.1kHz output sample, not per phi2 cycle. Not cycle-deterministic. CONFIRMED.
[14] SID filter variants: 6581 and 8580 are the same SVF with tweaked coefficients, not reSID two separate models. Sid8580D is a memoryless gain-scaler stub. CONFIRMED.
[15] SID external filter (extfilt): absent entirely. C64 output 16kHz low-pass + 16Hz DC-blocking high-pass missing. CONFIRMED.
[16] SID cutoff mapping: hand-authored piecewise-linear Hz table vs reSID f0_dac R-2R nonlinearity; 6581 cutoff kinks absent. CONFIRMED.
[17] SID resonance: invented linear 1/(1+res/4) vs reSID inverted-res nonlinear table-driven gain; res=15 near-self-oscillation not modeled. CONFIRMED.

Snapshot.Title: VIC-II + SID VICE-fidelity audit: divergences from viciisc/reSID
Description: [01] SID scope: reSID at native/vice/vice/src/resid is the specification. Live impl is src/ViceSharp.Chips/Audio/Sid6581.cs (+Sid8580,Sid8580D). Sid/Mos6581.cs and SidOscillator.cs are dead/unused.

[02] SID envelope FAITHFUL: rate_counter_period, sustain_level, exponential thresholds, the 0x8000 ADSR delay bug, the three pipelines, and register-write logic are bit-exact vs reSID envelope. The only faithful SID subsystem.

[03] SID envelope minor divergences: power-up counter seeded 0x00 vs reSID 0xaa (first-attack length + idle ENV3); envelope OUTPUT applied linearly with no model_dac; dead AttackRates/DecayReleaseRates tables hold wrong values; ProcessEnvelope comment wrongly says batched/SAMPLE_FAST.
[04] SID waveform combined: naive bitwise AND; reSID uses measured ROM tables (wave6581_*, wave8580_*) NOT ported. All combined waveforms wrong. Sid6581.cs:202-206 vs wave.h:458-498. CONFIRMED.
[05] SID waveform pulse: duty inverted. Managed HIGH when phase<pw; reSID HIGH when acc>>12>=pw. Exact opposites (pw=0: managed silent, reSID constant-high). Sid6581.cs:169 vs wave.h:243. CONFIRMED.

[06] SID waveform ring-mod: managed XORs whole triangle output on modulator MSB; reSID substitutes the triangle fold MSB and gates on sawtooth deselected. Wrong operation, polarity, gating. CONFIRMED.
[07] SID waveform hard-sync: managed resets on falling MSB edge; reSID resets on rising MSB edge (msb_rising). Opposite edge; missing same-cycle sync-source special case. CONFIRMED.

[08] SID noise LFSR: single register shared across all 3 voices (should be per-voice); runs only when noise selected (should free-run); no 2-cycle shift pipeline; no combined-waveform LFSR lock-up. CONFIRMED.
[09] SID TEST bit: instant LFSR reseed to 0x7FFFFF vs reSID ~35000-cycle fade; pulse not forced high during test; no falling-edge single clock. CONFIRMED.
[10] SID OSC3 ($D41B): returns raw accumulator phase for all non-sawtooth waveforms; should return selected waveform output. This is why the sawtooth-only parity test passes. CONFIRMED.
[11] SID resolution: 8-bit waveform path throughout vs reSID 12-bit + model_dac R-2R DAC. 4 bits + DAC nonlinearity lost. CONFIRMED.

[12] SID filter: generic Chamberlin state-variable filter. NONE of reSID op-amp spline/opamp_rev, cutoff-DAC/build_dac, EKV/VCR integrator, or resonance/mixer/gain tables exist. Structural, cannot be tuned to match. Sid6581.cs:282-365. CONFIRMED.
[13] SID filter clocking: integrated once per 44.1kHz output sample, not per phi2 cycle. Not cycle-deterministic. CONFIRMED.
[14] SID filter variants: 6581 and 8580 are the same SVF with tweaked coefficients, not reSID two separate models. Sid8580D is a memoryless gain-scaler stub. CONFIRMED.
[15] SID external filter (extfilt): absent entirely. C64 output 16kHz low-pass + 16Hz DC-blocking high-pass missing. CONFIRMED.
[16] SID cutoff mapping: hand-authored piecewise-linear Hz table vs reSID f0_dac R-2R nonlinearity; 6581 cutoff kinks absent. CONFIRMED.
[17] SID resonance: invented linear 1/(1+res/4) vs reSID inverted-res nonlinear table-driven gain; res=15 near-self-oscillation not modeled. CONFIRMED.
[18] SID volume/mixer: linear scalar vs reSID nonlinear gain[vol] op-amp DAC; digi is a fabricated DC constant not the mixer nonlinearity. CONFIRMED.
[19] SID voice-3 disconnect ($D418 bit7 / 3OFF): dropped (control masked 0x70). V3-mute is a no-op; voice 3 stays audible. Audible bug. CONFIRMED.
[20] SID output resampling: bare point-decimation (one cycle per ~22), no band-limiting FIR; cruder than reSID SAMPLE_FAST. CONFIRMED.
[21] SID databus/TTL: no bus_value fade (6581 0x1d00 / 8580 0xa2000); write-only registers read stored byte forever; SID-detect wrong. CONFIRMED.
[22] SID POT ($D419/$D41A): returns 0x00 vs reSID 0xFF; no paddle timing. CONFIRMED.
[23] SID 8580 write pipeline (1-cycle delay) not modeled; amplify scaleFactor (6581=3,8580=5) absent so relative loudness wrong. CONFIRMED.

[24] SID tests give false confidence: SidEngineParityTests is sawtooth-OSC3 only; SidCombinedWaveformTests asserts the naive-AND. Green SID tests validate the approximation. Must be replaced with reSID-derived exact-equality tests.
[25] VIC-II scope: viciisc at native/vice/vice/src/viciisc is the spec. Impl is VicIi/Mos6569.cs + VideoRenderer.cs + Core/C64MemoryMap.cs.

[26] VIC-II FAITHFUL: per-mode colour math (colors[]), register I/O masks + live read-backs, IRQ latch/enable + 9-bit raster compare, invalid-mode-to-black + priority bit, VC@13/RC@57 timing, g-fetch address math, refresh, sprite-DMA turn-on cycles, reset state.

[27] VIC-II render architecture (HEADLINE): whole-line geometric reconstruction (RenderRasterLine re-reads video RAM at line-end) vs VICE per-cycle 8px shift-register draw. Every mid-line change except $D020/$D021 lost; g-data re-read at render time so mid-line $D018 lost. CONFIRMED.

[28] VIC-II colour pipeline: no cregs one-pixel delay; no color_latency/grey-dot; $D022-$D02E mid-line changes lost; $D020/$D021 replay quantised to 8px boundaries with tuned FirstVisibleRasterX=12 vs DBUF_OFFSET geometry. CONFIRMED.
[29] VIC-II fine scroll: $D016 XSCROLL never applied to graphics pixels. CONFIRMED.
[30] VIC-II mode split: display mode/columns/colour sampled once per line; mid-line ECM/BMM/MCM/CSEL changes lost. CONFIRMED.
[31] VIC-II matrix addressing: screen row derived geometrically from raster, not the VC counter; diverges under vc/vcbase manipulation (FLD, DEN). CONFIRMED.
[32] VIC-II 38-column stride: reads screen[row*38+col] instead of row*40+col in 38-col mode (Mos6569.cs:1237). Wrong char/colour addresses. Concrete bug. CONFIRMED.
[33] VIC-II VC/VCBASE not reset at frame start (only Reset()); after frame 1 loads stale value. Breaks per-cycle lockstep. CONFIRMED.
[34] VIC-II bad-line off-by-one: allow_bad_lines cleared at >0xF8 not ==0xF7; one extra bad line at 0xF7 with YSCROLL==7. CONFIRMED.
[35] VIC-II DEN re-check: sampled once at line 0x30 start, not per-cycle; mid-line DEN enable on 0x30 missed. CONFIRMED.

[36] VIC-II c-access: one cycle late + collapsed with g-access (not pipelined); first 3 matrix slots hardcoded 0xFF/CPU-bus vs the prefetch_cycles counter, 3 wrong leading columns in lockstep buffer. CONFIRMED.
[37] VIC-II reg11 delay: BMM/ECM use current $D011 not last-cycle-delayed; 6569 char-ROM address-latch absent. CONFIRMED.
[38] VIC-II sprites rendering: whole-line geometric recompute from memory vs VICE per-pixel sbuf shift-register with xpos trigger + expansion/mc flip-flops. CONFIRMED.

[39] VIC-II sprites DMA: no mc/mcbase/exp_flop, no mcbase==63 stop, no display-bit latch; DMA a fixed 21/42-line window by line-counting; pointer/data read live at render time. Sprite crunch and mid-line $D017 not reproduced. CONFIRMED.
[40] VIC-II sprites collisions: once-per-line geometric with a single IRQ latch point, from a separate pass not the drawn pixels; per-pixel timing and border/off-screen collisions differ. CONFIRMED.
[41] VIC-II sprites multi-sprite priority: managed substitutes a lower-priority in-front sprite where VICE shows background (loop+continue vs winner-first). Behavioral bug. CONFIRMED.

[42] VIC-II border rendering: per-cycle main/vertical flip-flops feed only per-line boolean snapshots; border extent (geometry) + border colour ($D020 log) are two bolted approximations vs VICE single per-cycle draw_border8; no CSEL pixel-7 edge. CONFIRMED.
[43] VIC-II border-FF cycle base: LeftBorderCheckCycle 17/18 and RightBorderCheckCycle 56/57 are +1 vs VICE 0-based 16/17/55/56, inconsistent with correct VC@13/RC@57. CONFIRMED.
[44] VIC-II raster IRQ timing: fires one cycle late (RasterX==1 vs raster_cycle==0) for all lines except line 0. CONFIRMED.
[45] VIC-II raster IRQ re-arm: $D011/$D012 writes re-arm unconditionally (no unchanged-value guard, no raster_irq_triggered latch); handler can double-fire on same line. CONFIRMED.
[46] VIC-II collision clear: $D01E/$D01F cleared immediately on read vs VICE deferred to next cycle; no collision-enable gate. CONFIRMED (low).
[47] VIC-II light pen ($D013/$D014): X latch RasterX>>1 (0..31) vs VICE cycle_get_xpos/2 + x_extra_bits (~12..250); no delay, guards, frame retrigger, or old-6569R1 mode. CONFIRMED.
Snapshot.Remaining: S9/S10/S11 DONE. S12 (amplify/clip + external-filter enable, FR-SID-OUTPUT AC-01..07) DONE, ratchet 444->451: GenerateSample applies reSID amplify(scaleFactor 3/5)+integer clip on the pre-amplify SID::output() then /2^15 for the float host contract (6581 1.5x louder, matching VICE); ExternalFilter gained an enable flag (default true) with the disabled pass-through branch for AC-03. OUTPUT-01 composite lockstep vs the c64 oracle bit-exact; digi/lockstep/audio/determinism green. TR-SID-AMPLIFY-001 created. REMAINING: S13 (fixed-point Kaiser FIR resampler fast/interpolate/resample via the buffered oracle SidExactClockBuffered, FR-SID-OUTPUT AC-08..13, ratchet ->457; largest remaining piece, buffered export still unsmoked). Deferred cleanup: PLAN-SIDCHAMBERLIN-001. Non-SID: 9 unauthored parity ACs (other chip families) stay tracked.

[41] VIC-II sprites multi-sprite priority: managed substitutes a lower-priority in-front sprite where VICE shows background (loop+continue vs winner-first). Behavioral bug. CONFIRMED.

turns.queryText: I don't understand how there have been so many problems.  Need to go back to basics and audit the logic and edge cases of classic VICE and compare to managed and how things have gotten so far divergent.
turns.queryTitle: Audit classic VICE versus managed CPU architecture
turns.response: Completed a read-only architecture audit and stopped incremental CPU timing patching. Live evidence shows the managed CPU evolved from a 104-line instruction-granular engine with no phase flags to a 4,605-line hybrid with 95 phase booleans, 235 conditional branches, two execution paths, and predecessor-specific behavior. The functional opcode switch explicitly implements 180 of 256 values, omits decimal ADC/SBC and NMOS indirect-JMP wrap, and does not jam on JAM opcodes. Snapshot staging restarts in-flight CPU execution, lockstep compares only A/X/Y/S/P/Cycle/PC rather than bus events, and the hosted native C64 BA path bypasses VICE maincpu_steal_cycles bookkeeping. Diagnostic test receipt TestResults/cpu-visible-architecture-audit.trx records 140 passed, 8 failed, 0 skipped. Recommended remediation is to first prove and extend the native oracle, then replace the hybrid CPU with one VICE-macro-derived per-cycle micro-op engine covering all 256 opcodes and exhaustive bus/interrupt/steal edge cases before resuming xvic parity.

actions.description: Audited vendored VICE 6510dtvcore macro ordering, C64 and VIC-20 CLK_INC/FETCH paths, managed Mos6502 execution architecture, SystemClock steal handling, snapshot staging, and lockstep comparator.

dotnet test CpuVisiblePcTimingTests: 140 passed, 8 failed, 0 skipped, 148 total. Failures span stack/implied commit, branch fallthrough, store/JMP phase, immediate-load completion, compare flags, and IRQ clock accounting.

Suspend one-sample CPU timing patches. The managed core must return to VICE macro-derived per-cycle micro-operations with one authoritative state machine and bus-cycle oracle before Wolf64 or xvic parity work resumes.

CPU grew from 104 lines and 0 phase booleans before the VICE harness to 4605 lines and 95 phase booleans in the working tree. Current implementation contains dual instruction and staged-cycle engines, predecessor-history coupling, manual visible-PC projection, and incomplete reset of phase state.
Only 180 of 256 opcode values have explicit cases; 76 fall through. ADC/SBC ignore decimal mode, indirect JMP lacks NMOS page wrap, and JAM does not jam.

Lockstep equality compares A/X/Y/S/P/Cycle/PC only, not bus address, read/write/dummy type, opcode/micro-op, IRQ/NMI pipeline, or device-visible bus side effects. Snapshot staging reads native pipeline state but restarts managed CPU in-flight execution.

Hosted C64 check_ba path checkpoints stolen clocks by bypassing maincpu_steal_cycles, thereby omitting its REU, alarm, stolen-opcode, CLI/SEI, and interrupt-delay bookkeeping. Native reference must be repaired and proven before it remains the parity oracle.

processingDialog.content: Decision: Suspend incremental sample-specific CPU timing patches. Rationale: the managed instruction-granular core plus partial staged overlay, limited state-only oracle, and modified native steal path cannot establish VICE parity. Remediation starts with a proven native oracle and one VICE-macro-derived per-cycle micro-op engine. Rejected: continuing predecessor/opcode exception flags because each local correction has already regressed other pinned paths.

turns.queryText: Please pull the very oldest reqs about this project and tell me what it says about how vice-sharp should relate to VICE
turns.queryTitle: Recover original ViceSharp relationship to VICE
turns.response:
Yes. Your diagnosis is supported by the repository history.

The original model was correct:
- FRs defined observable emulator behavior, including FR-CPU-002 cycle-accurate instruction behavior and FR-VIC-001 PAL/NTSC raster timing, interrupts, and display/idle transitions.
- TR-CYCLE-001 defined the technical mechanism needed to satisfy those FRs: PHI1/PHI2 half-cycle execution, BA/AEC arbitration, per-cycle CPU pipeline state, deterministic device order, and VICE x64sc comparison.
- TEST requirements were supposed to prove every acceptance criterion against VICE x64sc and hardware-backed suites.

The later records broke that model. Commit e73a820 on 2026-05-27 regenerated the MCP wiki export and collapsed it from 219 FR headings, 40 TR headings, and 259 TEST lines to 12 FR headings, 9 TR headings, and 1 TEST line. It replaced the full FR-VIC-001 and TR-CYCLE-001 bodies with placeholders. Commit f608d02 on 2026-05-30 added narrow PAL 19,656-cycle checkpoint tests and tagged them with those legacy IDs. Commit d1cbf30 on 2026-05-31 then populated the placeholders from that narrow test wording.

There is evidence for the procedural reason: the work was a BACKFILL-VIDEO-001 traceability repair after the plan admitted that VICE behavior had not driven design before implementation. There is no recorded justification for reusing and narrowing the foundational IDs. Available May 27 background session records have zero persisted turns, so the decision rationale is absent.

Current MCP state confirms the damage:
- FR-VIC-001 and TR-CYCLE-001 are closed but each has zero acceptance criteria.
- FR-CPU-002 is absent.
- FR-VIC-006 and FR-VIC-010 are pending placeholders.
- The mapped tests prove narrow checkpoints, not the full original behavioral contract.

This proves a requirements and traceability failure. It does not by itself prove which runtime defects it caused, but it removed the coverage structure that should have prevented broad behavioral divergence while allowing narrow tests to appear green.

The original relationship to VICE was: ViceSharp may use an independent managed .NET architecture, but externally observable behavior and timing must match VICE x64sc and hardware evidence. VICE was the correctness oracle, not merely inspiration.

Independent review: PASS_WITH_QUALIFICATIONS, accuracy 100, completeness 100, 10 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 UNKNOWN. The FAIL is the current MCP contract loss. The UNKNOWNs are the missing rationale for ID reuse and direct causation of specific runtime defects.

Traced requirement drift: commit e73a820 (2026-05-27) collapsed the wiki export from 219 FR headings, 40 TR headings, and 259 TEST lines to 12 FR headings, 9 TR headings, and 1 TEST line, replacing full FR-VIC-001 and TR-CYCLE-001 bodies with placeholders.
Commit f608d02 (2026-05-30) added narrow PAL frame-periodic and cycle-counter tests annotated to legacy FR-VIC-001/TR-CYCLE-001 under BACKFILL-VIDEO-001.
Repository-wide git diff --check exits 2 because existing line 1567 has trailing whitespace. The historical requirements analysis did not modify this file.

Pinned the oldest requirement set to root commit d1f7175b70e0833ef9414faa98607130aa614da4 dated 2026-04-13 and inspected original FR-CPU, FR-Machine-Profiles, FR-Video-VIC-II, TR-CYCLE, TR-DET, TR-LIB, README, and architecture documents.

Commit d1cbf30 (2026-05-31) replaced the placeholder FR-VIC-001 and TR-CYCLE-001 records with narrow 19,656-cycle descriptions, while canonical docs/requirements retained the broad original contracts.

Live MCP has FR-VIC-001 and TR-CYCLE-001 closed with zero acceptance criteria, FR-CPU-002 absent, FR-VIC-006/010 as pending placeholders, and narrow TEST mappings. This does not preserve or prove the original foundational behavior contract.
Launched an independent historical-requirements review with durable request and response JSONL receipts and a 98 percent accuracy/completeness threshold.

processingDialog.content: Conclusion: the original ViceSharp contract treats VICE x64sc as the accepted behavioral correctness reference and gold standard for cycle-accurate C64 behavior, while separately requiring an idiomatic library-first .NET architecture. Consequence: internal managed structure may differ, but observable CPU, bus, VIC-II, timing, and test-program output must be proven against VICE x64sc and hardware-backed test evidence.
Is there evidence of why the newer FR was created?

Interpret the newer record as the conflicting MCP TR-CYCLE-001 titled VIC-II cycle counter frame-periodic, then trace its creation rationale and ID reuse through Git, requirement exports, TODOs, and session history.
Behavior of the emulator should be FR. If that is being violated then gaps in testing will cause foundational failures.

Conclusion under validation: the May 2026 requirements backfill overwrote or repurposed broad TR-CYCLE-001 with a narrow observable VIC-II frame-period behavior. Observable behavior belongs under FR coverage, while TR-CYCLE-001 should preserve the cross-cutting half-cycle implementation contract. This ID collision can let narrow tests appear to satisfy broad correctness while leaving PHI1/PHI2, arbitration, DMA, stalls, and interleave unproved.

Conclusion: the newer FR-VIC-001 and TR-CYCLE-001 were not a deliberate broad redesign evidenced in Git. They arose during BACKFILL-VIDEO-001 after a 2026-05-27 MCP/wiki export replaced full requirements with placeholders; narrow May 30 checkpoint tests were then used to populate those legacy IDs on May 31. Consequence: observable emulator behavior must be restored to complete FRs with acceptance criteria, broad cycle-accuracy architecture must remain in TR-CYCLE-001, and TEST mappings must prove every FR/TR criterion rather than a single PAL frame counter check.

processingDialog.content: Observation: live MCP has 383 requirement records but only 381 unique IDs. The current canonical requirement markdown has 204 unique IDs, 125 of which are absent from live MCP. The last intact pre-collapse export has 138 unique records, 112 absent from live MCP. Live MCP has 293 zero-acceptance records, 25 unmapped functional requirements, two cross-type duplicate TEST IDs, and 115 mappings whose currently named references resolve. Current canonical markdown preserves every pre-collapse record except TR-AOT-001.

Decision: do not restore by importing a historical wiki or replacing the live database. Build a per-ID recovery ledger and merge original broad behavior contracts with legitimate later additions. Observable emulator behavior remains FR, architecture/mechanism remains TR, and executable VICE differential proof remains TEST. Restore broad foundational IDs and move narrow checkpoint wording into acceptance criteria and scoped TR/TEST records. No requirements or code mutation occurs before plan approval.

Observation: current long xvic Fact tests return without assertion when vice_xvic is unavailable or VICESHARP_LOCKSTEP_10S/VICESHARP_LOCKSTEP_2S is unset, so ordinary green counts can include unexecuted required behavior. The every-cycle comparator asserts CPU A/X/Y/S/P/PC plus VIC-I video state, not full bus address/data/read-write, VIA, IRQ/NMI, audio, memory, and device side effects. Avalonia Settings binds VIC-20 panels to IsVic20Selected, but SelectedMachineProfile does not notify that derived property; existing UI tests only inspect source strings and property existence.

Correction to the earlier historical-count observation: the first parser wrongly required adjacent ID and Title fields and undercounted the pre-collapse canonical requirement corpus. Recomputed from commit d28493a using docs/requirements/functional/*.md, technical/*.md, and test/TEST-Requirements.md, parsing explicit **ID:** fields plus TEST requirement headings while excluding the document-title heading: 144 unique requirements total (108 FR, 17 TR, 19 TEST), with 114 absent from the live MCP store (88 FR, 10 TR, 16 TEST). The earlier 138/112 numbers are withdrawn and must not be used.

Correction to the earlier current-canonical count: a heading-only parser reported 204 because it omitted three legitimate explicit-ID definitions with non-ID headings (FR-WARP-001, TR-HOST-PRG-001, TR-WARP-STATUS-001) and included heading-only FR-XBOXGPL-007, which lacks an **ID:** field and is retired from active scope with UWP/Xbox. The active canonical source therefore has 206 explicit requirement definitions (129 FR, 36 TR, 41 TEST); 125 of those are absent from live MCP (92 FR, 13 TR, 20 TEST). A headings-plus-ID union is 207 only if the retired Xbox branding heading is included.

Live MCP TODO PLAN-REQAUDIT-001 remains open (created 2026-07-02T02:43:35.4437531Z). Its durable description already requires a complete FR/TR/TEST audit, VICE-derived acceptance criteria verified by running VICE, Byrd v4 red-first TDD, 100 percent green, and states: VICE is the specification; any vice# behavior that diverges from VICE is a bug, including where the same bug exists in VICE. This directly supports using the existing TODO as the recovery program umbrella rather than creating a competing plan before owner approval.

Hostile R1 correctly downgraded the May 27 causal claim. Evidence proves the generated export was incomplete/collapsed, but does not distinguish an already incomplete pre-export MCP database from a historical exporter defect. The cause is UNKNOWN; recovery must be source-agnostic. The prior statement that the database was already incomplete is withdrawn.

Requirement absence counts need two explicit semantics. Against live MCP IDs regardless of type, d28493a has 114 absent and current active canonical has 125 absent. Against the required same type, the counts are 115 and 126 because TEST-VIC-001 exists only as a wrongly TR-typed placeholder, not as a TEST record. The recovery ledger and completion gate must use same-type identity and repair this mismatch.

Gate requirements writes on an owner-approved recovery ledger and staged rollback-safe preview.

## Hostile validation

2026-09-23T18:48:20Z, Codex / GPT-6 Astra xhigh. **OverallVerdict: DISAGREE. Accuracy: 87.5%. Completeness: 25%.**

Accuracy is the conservative claim-verification score: 7 of 8 claims fully substantiated, with UNKNOWN receiving no credit. Completeness measures the four plan acceptance criteria: only the idle criterion is fully demonstrated; the shared input path is verified only up to the failure. Both scores are below the required 98%.

Scope classification: review of project implementation; workspace, Byrd, requirements, and plan gates apply.

Reviewed HEAD `687b03a75c1971bdb4bcbe07f2b5ea2d94f47b0d` plus the working tree. All 19 eligible profile Markdown files were read in full first, and reread after automatic compaction using add-profile. No product source was changed. The five initially hashed CPU, clock, timing-test, and validator files retained their hashes.

**Per-claim verdicts**

- **C1: PASS.** The 4146007 dump records native `S=F8 PC=A5FD nLastOp=B9 nIrqDelay=7`, against managed `S=F9 PC=A5F9 irqSeq=6 mDelays=True` (D/`wolf64-after-4139089-pbcskip.txt:28-31,44-47`). VICE executes `DO_INTERRUPT` before `FETCH_OPCODE` (`6510dtvcore.c:1758-1766,1804`). Its IRQ path performs two dummy clocks before pushing (`:388-405`), and DELAYS raises the threshold rather than enabling the check (`mainc64cpu.c:711-730`). The diagnosis is VICE-faithful.

- **C2: UNKNOWN as a complete VICE-faithfulness claim.** The pre-FETCH check is present before opcode replacement (`Mos6502.cs:1048-1065`); the stolen STA/LDA exceptions and STA zp cycle-zero notification are present (`:222-244,305-323,2297-2333`). The named pin passed, and my rebuilt Wolf64 run passed 4146007. The narrow correction is supported. However, “STORE/GET_ZERO is not DO_INTERRUPT” does not itself justify skipping the *following* instruction-boundary check. VICE still returns to its interrupt check after an instruction finishes. A skip is justified when execution has already passed that check and is suspended inside FETCH/check_ba; that distinction must be demonstrated. The current guards encode opcode/cycle history without an explicit “interrupt check already consumed” phase. The managed-only stolen-cycle pins do not independently establish that equivalence (`CpuVisiblePcTimingTests.cs:1550,1614,3181`). The BPL pin also accepts either IRQ arming or a stack decrement within eight steps and does not assert the exact pushed return address or first IRQ clock (`:4193-4207`). **4146007 diagnosis: faithful; pre-FETCH correction: supported; complete solution: INCOMPLETE.** This is not a claim that my live run regressed at 4146007.

- **C3: PASS.** The old 4147654 dump shows page-cross SBC at `A5BC` holding its opcode PC, then BEQ at `A5BF`; the final comparison has managed `A5C1`, native `A5BF`, and `P=A0`, so BEQ is not taken (D/`wolf64-after-4146007-stazp0.txt:42-47`). The current code retains the fuse state through absolute ALU handling and explicitly prevents that state from overriding this hold (`Mos6502.cs:1151-1158,1650-1687,1746-1752`). The causal explanation agrees with the code and dump.

- **C4: PASS for this scoped correction.** `_notTakenBranchHoldFinalPc` now survives the absolute-ALU predecessor, and its application exports the branch opcode PC (`Mos6502.cs:1154-1158,3177-3194`). VICE exports registers inside the second FETCH clock, before executing BRANCH's `INC_PC(2)` (`c64cpusc.c:58-68,149-174`; `6510dtvcore.c:986-1005`). The named BEQ pin passed; my live run passed 4147654 and failed at 4147669. **The 4147654 diagnosis and narrow hold solution are VICE-faithful.** This does not establish every absolute-ALU/branch combination.

- **C5: PASS for the current-state and retained-regression evidence.** My live run independently reproduced **FirstMismatchCycle=4147669**: managed `PC=A5FA Y=CE P=A1`; native `PC=A5F9 Y=CD P=21`, with `nLastOp=C8` (E/`wolf64.stdout.txt:8-11,27`). The supplied post-attempt dump fails at 4138197, where managed LDA still has `A=DC` while native has `A=50`; its preceding INY deferred-completion tick is visible (D/`wolf64-after-4147669.txt:28,40-47`). The current defer assignment does not include the proposed INC-after-full-branch addition (`Mos6502.cs:1292`). I did not restore or replay the historical patch. 4147669 remains open.

turns.queryTitle: Audit classic VICE versus managed CPU architecture
turns.response: Completed a read-only architecture audit and stopped incremental CPU timing patching. Live evidence shows the managed CPU evolved from a 104-line instruction-granular engine with no phase flags to a 4,605-line hybrid with 95 phase booleans, 235 conditional branches, two execution paths, and predecessor-specific behavior. The functional opcode switch explicitly implements 180 of 256 values, omits decimal ADC/SBC and NMOS indirect-JMP wrap, and does not jam on JAM opcodes. Snapshot staging restarts in-flight CPU execution, lockstep compares only A/X/Y/S/P/Cycle/PC rather than bus events, and the hosted native C64 BA path bypasses VICE maincpu_steal_cycles bookkeeping. Diagnostic test receipt TestResults/cpu-visible-architecture-audit.trx records 140 passed, 8 failed, 0 skipped. Recommended remediation is to first prove and extend the native oracle, then replace the hybrid CPU with one VICE-macro-derived per-cycle micro-op engine covering all 256 opcodes and exhaustive bus/interrupt/steal edge cases before resuming xvic parity.

CPU grew from 104 lines and 0 phase booleans before the VICE harness to 4605 lines and 95 phase booleans in the working tree. Current implementation contains dual instruction and staged-cycle engines, predecessor-history coupling, manual visible-PC projection, and incomplete reset of phase state.
Only 180 of 256 opcode values have explicit cases; 76 fall through. ADC/SBC ignore decimal mode, indirect JMP lacks NMOS page wrap, and JAM does not jam.

Lockstep equality compares A/X/Y/S/P/Cycle/PC only, not bus address, read/write/dummy type, opcode/micro-op, IRQ/NMI pipeline, or device-visible bus side effects. Snapshot staging reads native pipeline state but restarts managed CPU in-flight execution.

Hosted C64 check_ba path checkpoints stolen clocks by bypassing maincpu_steal_cycles, thereby omitting its REU, alarm, stolen-opcode, CLI/SEI, and interrupt-delay bookkeeping. Native reference must be repaired and proven before it remains the parity oracle.

Yes. Your diagnosis is supported by the repository history.

The original model was correct:
- FRs defined observable emulator behavior, including FR-CPU-002 cycle-accurate instruction behavior and FR-VIC-001 PAL/NTSC raster timing, interrupts, and display/idle transitions.
- TR-CYCLE-001 defined the technical mechanism needed to satisfy those FRs: PHI1/PHI2 half-cycle execution, BA/AEC arbitration, per-cycle CPU pipeline state, deterministic device order, and VICE x64sc comparison.
- TEST requirements were supposed to prove every acceptance criterion against VICE x64sc and hardware-backed suites.

The later records broke that model. Commit e73a820 on 2026-05-27 regenerated the MCP wiki export and collapsed it from 219 FR headings, 40 TR headings, and 259 TEST lines to 12 FR headings, 9 TR headings, and 1 TEST line. It replaced the full FR-VIC-001 and TR-CYCLE-001 bodies with placeholders. Commit f608d02 on 2026-05-30 added narrow PAL 19,656-cycle checkpoint tests and tagged them with those legacy IDs. Commit d1cbf30 on 2026-05-31 then populated the placeholders from that narrow test wording.

There is evidence for the procedural reason: the work was a BACKFILL-VIDEO-001 traceability repair after the plan admitted that VICE behavior had not driven design before implementation. There is no recorded justification for reusing and narrowing the foundational IDs. Available May 27 background session records have zero persisted turns, so the decision rationale is absent.

Current MCP state confirms the damage:
- FR-VIC-001 and TR-CYCLE-001 are closed but each has zero acceptance criteria.
- FR-CPU-002 is absent.
- FR-VIC-006 and FR-VIC-010 are pending placeholders.
- The mapped tests prove narrow checkpoints, not the full original behavioral contract.

This proves a requirements and traceability failure. It does not by itself prove which runtime defects it caused, but it removed the coverage structure that should have prevented broad behavioral divergence while allowing narrow tests to appear green.

The original relationship to VICE was: ViceSharp may use an independent managed .NET architecture, but externally observable behavior and timing must match VICE x64sc and hardware evidence. VICE was the correctness oracle, not merely inspiration.

processingDialog.content: Observation: live MCP has 383 requirement records but only 381 unique IDs. The current canonical requirement markdown has 204 unique IDs, 125 of which are absent from live MCP. The last intact pre-collapse export has 138 unique records, 112 absent from live MCP. Live MCP has 293 zero-acceptance records, 25 unmapped functional requirements, two cross-type duplicate TEST IDs, and 115 mappings whose currently named references resolve. Current canonical markdown preserves every pre-collapse record except TR-AOT-001.

Decision: do not restore by importing a historical wiki or replacing the live database. Build a per-ID recovery ledger and merge original broad behavior contracts with legitimate later additions. Observable emulator behavior remains FR, architecture/mechanism remains TR, and executable VICE differential proof remains TEST. Restore broad foundational IDs and move narrow checkpoint wording into acceptance criteria and scoped TR/TEST records. No requirements or code mutation occurs before plan approval.

Observation: current long xvic Fact tests return without assertion when vice_xvic is unavailable or VICESHARP_LOCKSTEP_10S/VICESHARP_LOCKSTEP_2S is unset, so ordinary green counts can include unexecuted required behavior. The every-cycle comparator asserts CPU A/X/Y/S/P/PC plus VIC-I video state, not full bus address/data/read-write, VIA, IRQ/NMI, audio, memory, and device side effects. Avalonia Settings binds VIC-20 panels to IsVic20Selected, but SelectedMachineProfile does not notify that derived property; existing UI tests only inspect source strings and property existence.

Correction to the earlier historical-count observation: the first parser wrongly required adjacent ID and Title fields and undercounted the pre-collapse canonical requirement corpus. Recomputed from commit d28493a using docs/requirements/functional/*.md, technical/*.md, and test/TEST-Requirements.md, parsing explicit **ID:** fields plus TEST requirement headings while excluding the document-title heading: 144 unique requirements total (108 FR, 17 TR, 19 TEST), with 114 absent from the live MCP store (88 FR, 10 TR, 16 TEST). The earlier 138/112 numbers are withdrawn and must not be used.

Correction to the earlier current-canonical count: a heading-only parser reported 204 because it omitted three legitimate explicit-ID definitions with non-ID headings (FR-WARP-001, TR-HOST-PRG-001, TR-WARP-STATUS-001) and included heading-only FR-XBOXGPL-007, which lacks an **ID:** field and is retired from active scope with UWP/Xbox. The active canonical source therefore has 206 explicit requirement definitions (129 FR, 36 TR, 41 TEST); 125 of those are absent from live MCP (92 FR, 13 TR, 20 TEST). A headings-plus-ID union is 207 only if the retired Xbox branding heading is included.

Live MCP TODO PLAN-REQAUDIT-001 remains open (created 2026-07-02T02:43:35.4437531Z). Its durable description already requires a complete FR/TR/TEST audit, VICE-derived acceptance criteria verified by running VICE, Byrd v4 red-first TDD, 100 percent green, and states: VICE is the specification; any vice# behavior that diverges from VICE is a bug, including where the same bug exists in VICE. This directly supports using the existing TODO as the recovery program umbrella rather than creating a competing plan before owner approval.

Hostile R1 correctly downgraded the May 27 causal claim. Evidence proves the generated export was incomplete/collapsed, but does not distinguish an already incomplete pre-export MCP database from a historical exporter defect. The cause is UNKNOWN; recovery must be source-agnostic. The prior statement that the database was already incomplete is withdrawn.

Requirement absence counts need two explicit semantics. Against live MCP IDs regardless of type, d28493a has 114 absent and current active canonical has 125 absent. Against the required same type, the counts are 115 and 126 because TEST-VIC-001 exists only as a wrongly TR-typed placeholder, not as a TEST record. The recovery ledger and completion gate must use same-type identity and repair this mismatch.

# Refresh Docs

Reconcile `docs/` with the current codebase, remove documentation that no longer applies, make `docs/wiki.yaml` list every project doc that should be published to the wiki, and export the MCP-backed requirement documents.

## Preconditions

- Work from the repository root.
- Read `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` and follow its marker, plugin, session, and trust rules. Verify the marker signature and the `/health` nonce before any MCP mutation.
- Use the required MCP Server plugin for your agent (Claude/Codex/Grok) for requirements and export (`workflow.requirements.*`). Do not hand-author exported requirement docs or substitute raw REST.
- Use the operator's approved shell for all shell invocation (e.g. PowerShell.Mcp on Windows). Build YAML/JSON from native objects and serialize; never handwrite fragile payloads.
- Read facts from the code, not from memory. This skill refreshes and exports only; it does not commit or push (leave that to a wrap-up flow or an explicit request).

## Step 1 - Refresh project documentation

1. Inventory the docs surface: `docs/user/*`, `docs/architecture/*`, `docs/requirements/*.md`, `docs/testing/*`, `docs/*.md`, and `README.md` (adapt to the repo's actual layout).
2. Establish what changed since the docs were last touched: `git log --oneline` for the changed code areas, the current project/solution structure, public commands, and settings. Prefer the shipped behavior over any doc's prior claims.
3. Update each doc that drifted: renamed or removed components, changed UI/behavior, new or removed features, install commands and version pins, and cross-references. Match the existing doc voice; no em-dashes.
4. Keep the project `README.md` current as a first-class refresh target, not an afterthought: the project description and overview, the feature list, install and quickstart/usage commands, current version references, badges, and links into `docs/` must all match the shipped state. Reconcile it against the code and the refreshed docs on every run.
5. If the repo ships a documentation screenshot/capture script (for example `scripts/Capture-ClientToolScreenshots.ps1`) and the UI changed, regenerate the embedded screenshots into the docs image folder from the current build, and verify a raw capture reflects the current UI before keeping it.

## Step 2 - Prune out-of-date docs

1. Find docs describing removed or superseded features: grep the docs for names of deleted components, APIs, or flows and confirm against the code that they no longer exist.
2. Delete the obsolete `.md` files, and remove their references from index pages (for example `docs/user/index.md`) and from `docs/wiki.yaml`.
3. Do not delete a doc that still has accurate content. When a doc is partly stale, update it rather than delete. When unsure whether to remove a doc, flag it in the report instead of deleting.

## Step 3 - Update docs/wiki.yaml

`docs/wiki.yaml` uses schema `mcp-wiki-export/v1` with `home.document`, a `documents` list, and a `navigation` tree. Each `documents` entry is `{ id, title, source, target, platforms }`.

1. Keep the server-generated requirement docs (their `source` is `generated:<key>`, for example `generated:home|functional|technical|testing|mapping|matrix`). Do not point these at files.
2. Add or refresh a `documents` entry for every CURRENT project doc that should appear in the wiki (the user guides under `docs/user/` and the architecture docs under `docs/architecture/`, plus `docs/Development-Process.md` / `README.md` if desired):
   - `source`: the repo-relative path to the markdown file, for example `docs/user/client-tool.md`.
   - `target`: the wiki page filename in PascalCase-with-hyphens, for example `Client-Tool.md`.
   - `title`: the human page title.
   - `platforms`: `[github, azure]` unless a doc is platform-specific.
   Use stable `id` slugs (for example `user-client-tool`, `arch-overview`).
3. Remove `documents` and `navigation` entries for any doc pruned in Step 2 or no longer present on disk.
4. Add each new document to `navigation` (as a child of the appropriate parent, or top-level). Keep the generated requirement docs grouped as they are.
5. If the repo has a wiki sync script (for example `scripts/Sync-GitHubWikiDocs.ps1`) with its own project-doc list, cross-check it against `docs/wiki.yaml` so the manifest and the sync script agree on which project docs publish and their page names.
6. Confirm the file still parses as YAML after editing.

## Step 4 - Export requirements

1. Export via the MCP requirements workflow: `workflow.requirements.generateDocument` with `format: wiki` and `docType: all`.
2. Write the returned `contentBase64` ZIP exactly to `docs/requirements/requirements-wiki-documents.zip`. The MCP database is the source of truth; do not hand-author the exported docs.
3. If the server also regenerates in-place markdown under `docs/Project/wiki/`, review the diff. Keep only the intended requirement changes. Do NOT accept destructive deletions of project-doc wiki pages that are listed in `docs/wiki.yaml`; that means the manifest and the export disagree, so fix `docs/wiki.yaml` in Step 3 rather than accept the deletions.
4. If the server rejects `format: wiki`, record it as a blocker and stop; do not fall back to another format unless the user asks.

## Validation and report

- Run `git diff --check`; confirm `docs/wiki.yaml` parses; if code samples in docs changed, sanity-build the relevant snippet.
- Report only verified facts: `README.md` updated, docs updated, docs pruned (with reasons), `docs/wiki.yaml` entries added/removed, screenshots regenerated, the requirements export artifact path, and any docs you flagged instead of deleting or any blockers.
- Do not commit or push; summarize the changes and let the operator run a wrap-up or commit explicitly.


**ARGUMENTS:** and
</skill>
<skill name="mcpserver:wrap-up" args="with detailed handoff">
Finish and synchronize MCP-backed work: reconcile requirements, export wiki documents, run validation, commit/push, and close out the session-log turn.

## Trust and transport

Trust marker details only after the plugin's local status/bootstrap check confirms marker trust and workspace health (including signature and nonce health). Use the plugin's supported wrapper surface for MCP mutations (for example `lib/repl-invoke.ps1`, or the plugin's session, todo, and requirements tools); do not use raw REST for normal MCP mutations.

## Method-name disambiguation

`workflow.*` names in this skill (`workflow.sessionlog.*`, `workflow.todo.*`, `workflow.requirements.*`) are plugin workflow/REPL method names, not literal native MCP tool names. Native `/mcp-transport` tools use names such as `sessionlog_*`, `todo_*`, and `requirements_*` (for example `sessionlog_submit`, `todo_list`, `requirements_generate`); hosted-agent adapters may expose `mcp_*` aliases. Do not declare the plugin unavailable solely because generic MCP discovery does not list literal `workflow.*` names.

If your agent exposes only a `pwsh` (or shell) tool, invoke the plugin shim directly instead of declaring it unavailable:

```
pwsh.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File "<plugin-root>\lib\repl-invoke.ps1" -Method <workflow.method> -ParamsYaml <yaml>
```

## Wrap-up steps

1. Reconcile requirements with `workflow.requirements.*`, including requirement reconciliation for new FR/TR/TEST evidence.
2. Export wiki requirements with `workflow.requirements.generateDocument` using `format: wiki` and `docType: all`.
3. Run validation commands and keep zero-failure zero-skip evidence.
4. If commit/push is required, use the `commit-sync` pause and acknowledgement contract first.
5. Perform session-log reconciliation with `workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog` and `workflow.sessionlog.appendActions`.
6. Finish with `workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn`; use `workflow.sessionlog.failTurn` when validation, export, or commit/push cannot be completed (validation failure, export failure, or blocked commit/push).


**ARGUMENTS:** with detailed handoff

You are the Goal Plan Writer for the xAI Grok Build harness. You run ONCE
at goal creation. Convert the objective into a structured plan that the
implementer, the adversarial verifiers, and the classifier use as the single
source of truth for "what was supposed to happen". The user never sees it ΓÇö
write for those readers, some of which run on small models: keep it short,
concrete, and unambiguous.

## Inputs (below this prompt)

- OBJECTIVE: the user's goal, verbatim.
- CONTEXT: optional extra snippet (usually empty). Parent implementer history
  arrives as a forked conversation prefix (`<background_context>`), not here.

Inspect files named in OBJECTIVE/CONTEXT with your
`read_file`/`grep`/`list_dir` tools to clarify scope. Do NOT modify
the workspace; your only write is `C:\Users\kingd\.grok\sessions\F%3A%5CGitHub%5Cvice-sharp\019fd0df-383d-7fc0-9f0a-69785afd78ed\goal\plan.md`.

When the OBJECTIVE names something with an established canon or spec ΓÇö a named
game or "classic X", a named algorithm/protocol/format, a "clone of <a specific
product>" ΓÇö and web access is available, FIRST research it with your
`web_search` tool (and `web_fetch` to open a source) to learn its
DEFINING mechanics before writing criteria; do NOT plan it from memory alone.
Defining mechanics are the PRIMARY behaviors without which the deliverable is
NOT recognizably that thing ΓÇö e.g. for a key-value store, durable get-after-set;
for a parser, round-trip of valid input; for a platformer, enemies that defeat /
are defeated by the player plus a win state and a lose state (NOT
error/edge/invalid-input handling, which stays a Non-goal unless the OBJECTIVE
states it). This applies ONLY to such named things; a generic archetype
("a todo app", "a REST API for a blog") is not a named artifact ΓÇö skip it.

Do not map one criterion per mechanic. Identify the defining mechanics, then
FOLD them into a SMALL criteria set by GROUPING related ones ΓÇö a single
criterion may name several closely-related mechanics that form ONE checkable
outcome (never a whole-system end-to-end gate) ΓÇö so the set fits the `## Acceptance
criteria` cap below (a ceiling, not a target to fill). Grouping, NOT dropping,
is how you fit the cap: never silently omit a core mechanic; if one genuinely
cannot fit, record it under `## Non-goals` (or `## Assumed scope`) as an
explicit deferral. For each candidate apply the test
"without it, is it still recognizably the named thing?": NO ΓåÆ core, it
belongs in the criteria, grouped if needed (unless the OBJECTIVE contradicts
it ΓÇö OBJECTIVE's explicit words always win); YES ΓåÆ polish, fidelity, or extra
scope: list it under `## Non-goals` (e.g. for a platformer, power-ups or
score) so the verifier sees it was deferred, not forgotten. If web research
is unavailable or fails, note the gap under `## Assumed scope` and proceed
from best knowledge.

## Goal kind ΓÇö pick exactly one

- `code-change` ΓÇö modify the workspace; the diff is the evidence.
- `analysis` ΓÇö understand existing code; deliverable is prose, diff may be empty.
- `research` ΓÇö gather external info; deliverable is a summary, diff may be empty.

## Specify OUTCOMES, not architecture

The frozen plan is a contract on the OBSERVABLE OUTCOME the objective asks for,
NOT on how to build it. You MUST NOT prescribe the module/file layout, class or
function names, or exact signatures ΓÇö freezing the HOW pins one solution and
lets the verifier refute correct work for diverging from it. State each criterion
as an outcome the objective implies ("the core parseΓåÆnormalize transform can be
exercised directly on representative inputs" ΓÇö GOOD), never as a named artifact
("a `parser.py` exporting `normalize(record, opts)`" ΓÇö BAD).

## Visual / interactive objectives

When the deliverable is primarily visual or interactive (a game, a canvas/UI
app, a browser page ΓÇö e.g. "implement a platformer in JS"), the harness cannot
drive it end-to-end. Do NOT write criteria that require playing or watching it.
Instead anchor the criteria on the static/structural fallback: the artifact
exists in the source (the page, the game loop, the named controls/bindings the
objective lists ΓÇö keep them verbatim), the pure logic units (physics,
collision, input mapping, state transitions) are exercised directly by real
unit tests, AND every browser-loaded script provably loads in a browser-like
environment ΓÇö e.g. evaluate it headlessly with a `window` global defined and
NO Node globals (`module`, `require`), asserting it executes without error and
installs its expected globals. A script that only loads under Node (an
unguarded `module.exports`) renders a black page and fails the objective.
Prefer artifacts that work when the page is opened DIRECTLY from disk (plain

modules/import-map page is a silent black screen when double-clicked. If ES
modules are genuinely needed, the page MUST detect `file:` and display how to
serve it instead of failing silently.

## Entry-point launch check ΓÇö all runnable deliverables

Unit tests of internals do NOT prove the deliverable starts: a missing import
map, a crashing `main()`, or a bad entry script all pass unit tests and fail
the user on first launch. Whenever the deliverable has a launchable entry
point and the environment can run it, the verification plan MUST include one
GATING launch on the real entry path with the cheapest available runtime,
asserting NOT merely that it starts but that its PRIMARY OBSERVABLE is CORRECT

`{SCRATCH}`. Run the launch MORE THAN ONCE and assert CONSISTENT success:
non-deterministic launch output (a pass on one run, an empty/error capture on
the next) is an APP-side defect to FIX, not to average away or
cherry-pick a success from (if the ENVIRONMENT is what's flaky, capture that

  surface ΓÇö NOT a `> 0 pixels` check),
  and a driven input produces the expected visible change; capture a
  screenshot. Module-resolution mistakes (bare specifiers, import maps) surface
  ONLY on a real page load.

Degradation MUST be honest, never fabricated: if the launch tool itself fails
for environmental reasons (e.g. the headless browser cannot install or start
in this sandbox, or it can start but
cannot reliably read back the primary observable ΓÇö headless pixel readback or
input injection unavailable), the implementer captures THAT failure output to
`{SCRATCH}` and the static/structural fallback + unit tests become the
accepted bar ΓÇö
write this escape hatch INTO the launch step ("...or captured evidence the
launcher cannot run here"). A readback that SUCCEEDS and returns a blank or
partial buffer is the app's output, not an unavailable readback ΓÇö fix it, do
not fall back. Synthetic/hand-built stand-ins for launch evidence
are worse than the honest fallback and will be refuted. When the environment
clearly cannot launch the deliverable at all, plan the fallback directly and
record the limit under `## Risks / Contradictions`. Verification steps may add capturable evidence (a screenshot, a DOM
dump, a headless-run log) as `evidence`, never as `gating`.

## Output contract ΓÇö STRICT

Use your `write` tool to write Markdown to `C:\Users\kingd\.grok\sessions\F%3A%5CGitHub%5Cvice-sharp\019fd0df-383d-7fc0-9f0a-69785afd78ed\goal\plan.md` with these
sections, in order. `## Implementation approach` and `## Task checklist` are
`code-change` only; include `## Risks / Contradictions` only when one exists.

```

## Goal kind
<code-change | analysis | research>

## Acceptance criteria
1. <gating, outcome-based criterion>

## Verification plan
1. <gating|evidence: action + the observations that MUST be present to pass>

## Non-goals
- <out-of-scope item>

## Assumed scope
<files / modules / external deps this goal touches>

## Implementation approach
<code-change only: how to structure the code so it is easy to test>

## Task checklist
- [ ] <code-change only: first concrete implementation step>
- [ ] <next step>

## Risks / Contradictions
```

**Acceptance criteria** ΓÇö these are the GATING set: every one must hold to pass,
so keep it SMALL (aim 3-5) and satisficing, never an exhaustive conjunction.
Numbered, concrete, one outcome each, anchored to the LITERAL objective:
do NOT invent scope. A reasonable-but-unrequested feature goes under `## Non-goals`,
never here (but a DEFINING mechanic of an artifact the OBJECTIVE names is implied
by that name ΓÇö it is requested, so it stays here) ΓÇö inflating the contract is what
makes a goal unfinishable. Each
criterion must be atomic and independently checkable from near its own start
state: never write a single holistic end-to-end gate ("drive the whole thing
through to the end"), which an automated check rarely completes ΓÇö decompose into
separate checks. Preserve OBJECTIVE's must-have terms verbatim: never swap a
named technique, technology, or artifact for an easier one; if a must-have seems
wrong or infeasible, keep it AND record the conflict under `## Risks /
Contradictions`.

both follow, so all judge by the SAME observable bar; cover every criterion.
Tag each step `gating` (decides pass/fail) or `evidence` (best-effort
corroboration whose absence alone, once the gating steps and honest unit checks
hold, must NOT deny completion). Each step gives the **action** (run the tests,
exercise the entry point, read the artifact) and the
**observations that MUST be** present to pass. Rules:

- Drive the REAL shipped functions/entry points from their real start state ΓÇö
  not a copy, a re-implementation, or a scenario starting past the thing checked.
- Static / structural fallback ΓÇö the BLESSED path when behavior cannot be driven
  here (a UI, a browser, a long-running interactive session): do NOT prescribe a
  flaky end-to-end run, a specific capture-file ritual, or an end-to-end outcome
  ("reach the end state") proven through test-only scaffolding. Require only the
  MINIMAL honest path: the artifact EXISTS in the source AND the shipped

- Output paths use the literal `{SCRATCH}` placeholder (e.g. `{SCRATCH}/out.log`),

**Risks / Contradictions** (optional) ΓÇö one bullet per genuine internal

You are the Goal Plan Writer for the xAI Grok Build harness. You run ONCE
at goal creation. Convert the objective into a structured plan that the
implementer, the adversarial verifiers, and the classifier use as the single
source of truth for "what was supposed to happen". The user never sees it ΓÇö
write for those readers, some of which run on small models: keep it short,
concrete, and unambiguous.

## Inputs (below this prompt)

- OBJECTIVE: the user's goal, verbatim.
- CONTEXT: optional extra snippet (usually empty). Parent implementer history
  arrives as a forked conversation prefix (`<background_context>`), not here.

Inspect files named in OBJECTIVE/CONTEXT with your
`read_file`/`grep`/`list_dir` tools to clarify scope. Do NOT modify
the workspace; your only write is `C:\Users\kingd\.grok\sessions\F%3A%5CGitHub%5Cvice-sharp\019fd0df-383d-7fc0-9f0a-69785afd78ed\goal\plan.md`.

When the OBJECTIVE names something with an established canon or spec ΓÇö a named
game or "classic X", a named algorithm/protocol/format, a "clone of <a specific
product>" ΓÇö and web access is available, FIRST research it with your
`web_search` tool (and `web_fetch` to open a source) to learn its
DEFINING mechanics before writing criteria; do NOT plan it from memory alone.
Defining mechanics are the PRIMARY behaviors without which the deliverable is
NOT recognizably that thing ΓÇö e.g. for a key-value store, durable get-after-set;
for a parser, round-trip of valid input; for a platformer, enemies that defeat /
are defeated by the player plus a win state and a lose state (NOT
error/edge/invalid-input handling, which stays a Non-goal unless the OBJECTIVE
states it). This applies ONLY to such named things; a generic archetype
("a todo app", "a REST API for a blog") is not a named artifact ΓÇö skip it.

Do not map one criterion per mechanic. Identify the defining mechanics, then
FOLD them into a SMALL criteria set by GROUPING related ones ΓÇö a single
criterion may name several closely-related mechanics that form ONE checkable
outcome (never a whole-system end-to-end gate) ΓÇö so the set fits the `## Acceptance
criteria` cap below (a ceiling, not a target to fill). Grouping, NOT dropping,
is how you fit the cap: never silently omit a core mechanic; if one genuinely
cannot fit, record it under `## Non-goals` (or `## Assumed scope`) as an
explicit deferral. For each candidate apply the test
"without it, is it still recognizably the named thing?": NO ΓåÆ core, it
belongs in the criteria, grouped if needed (unless the OBJECTIVE contradicts
it ΓÇö OBJECTIVE's explicit words always win); YES ΓåÆ polish, fidelity, or extra
scope: list it under `## Non-goals` (e.g. for a platformer, power-ups or
score) so the verifier sees it was deferred, not forgotten. If web research
is unavailable or fails, note the gap under `## Assumed scope` and proceed
from best knowledge.

## Goal kind ΓÇö pick exactly one

- `code-change` ΓÇö modify the workspace; the diff is the evidence.
- `analysis` ΓÇö understand existing code; deliverable is prose, diff may be empty.
- `research` ΓÇö gather external info; deliverable is a summary, diff may be empty.

## Specify OUTCOMES, not architecture

The frozen plan is a contract on the OBSERVABLE OUTCOME the objective asks for,
NOT on how to build it. You MUST NOT prescribe the module/file layout, class or
function names, or exact signatures ΓÇö freezing the HOW pins one solution and
lets the verifier refute correct work for diverging from it. State each criterion
as an outcome the objective implies ("the core parseΓåÆnormalize transform can be
exercised directly on representative inputs" ΓÇö GOOD), never as a named artifact
("a `parser.py` exporting `normalize(record, opts)`" ΓÇö BAD).

## Visual / interactive objectives

When the deliverable is primarily visual or interactive (a game, a canvas/UI
app, a browser page ΓÇö e.g. "implement a platformer in JS"), the harness cannot
drive it end-to-end. Do NOT write criteria that require playing or watching it.
Instead anchor the criteria on the static/structural fallback: the artifact
exists in the source (the page, the game loop, the named controls/bindings the
objective lists ΓÇö keep them verbatim), the pure logic units (physics,
collision, input mapping, state transitions) are exercised directly by real
unit tests, AND every browser-loaded script provably loads in a browser-like
environment ΓÇö e.g. evaluate it headlessly with a `window` global defined and
NO Node globals (`module`, `require`), asserting it executes without error and
installs its expected globals. A script that only loads under Node (an
unguarded `module.exports`) renders a black page and fails the objective.
Prefer artifacts that work when the page is opened DIRECTLY from disk (plain
`<script src>` over ES modules): `file://` blocks module imports by CORS, so a
modules/import-map page is a silent black screen when double-clicked. If ES
modules are genuinely needed, the page MUST detect `file:` and display how to
serve it instead of failing silently.

## Entry-point launch check ΓÇö all runnable deliverables

Unit tests of internals do NOT prove the deliverable starts: a missing import
map, a crashing `main()`, or a bad entry script all pass unit tests and fail
the user on first launch. Whenever the deliverable has a launchable entry
point and the environment can run it, the verification plan MUST include one
GATING launch on the real entry path with the cheapest available runtime,
asserting NOT merely that it starts but that its PRIMARY OBSERVABLE is CORRECT
(present and non-empty is INSUFFICIENT), and producing captured output in
`{SCRATCH}`. Run the launch MORE THAN ONCE and assert CONSISTENT success:
non-deterministic launch output (a pass on one run, an empty/error capture on
the next) is an APP-side defect to FIX, not to average away or
cherry-pick a success from (if the ENVIRONMENT is what's flaky, capture that
and take the honest fallback below). Assert the primary observable per
deliverable:

- CLI tool ΓåÆ run the real command on a representative input; assert the actual
  output CONTENT, not just that it ran; capture output.
- Server/service ΓåÆ boot it, hit one endpoint, assert the response BODY is sane,
  not just an HTTP 200.
- Library ΓåÆ import/load it from a fresh consumer (not only from its tests) and
  assert a real call's RETURN VALUE.
- Browser page ΓåÆ probe for a headless browser (e.g. `npx playwright
  --version`); if present, serve + load the page and assert zero page errors,
  the render surface's drawing dimensions equal the intended/target size
  (catches a renderer that cached a stale/default size), the surface is
  SUBSTANTIALLY filled (a high painted fraction or a painted bbox Γëê the whole
  surface ΓÇö NOT a `> 0 pixels` check),
  and a driven input produces the expected visible change; capture a
  screenshot. Module-resolution mistakes (bare specifiers, import maps) surface
  ONLY on a real page load.

Degradation MUST be honest, never fabricated: if the launch tool itself fails
for environmental reasons (e.g. the headless browser cannot install or start
in this sandbox, or it can start but
cannot reliably read back the primary observable ΓÇö headless pixel readback or
input injection unavailable), the implementer captures THAT failure output to
`{SCRATCH}` and the static/structural fallback + unit tests become the
accepted bar ΓÇö
write this escape hatch INTO the launch step ("...or captured evidence the
launcher cannot run here"). A readback that SUCCEEDS and returns a blank or
partial buffer is the app's output, not an unavailable readback ΓÇö fix it, do
not fall back. Synthetic/hand-built stand-ins for launch evidence
are worse than the honest fallback and will be refuted. When the environment
clearly cannot launch the deliverable at all, plan the fallback directly and
record the limit under `## Risks / Contradictions`. Verification steps may add capturable evidence (a screenshot, a DOM
dump, a headless-run log) as `evidence`, never as `gating`.

## Output contract ΓÇö STRICT

Use your `write` tool to write Markdown to `C:\Users\kingd\.grok\sessions\F%3A%5CGitHub%5Cvice-sharp\019fd0df-383d-7fc0-9f0a-69785afd78ed\goal\plan.md` with these
sections, in order. `## Implementation approach` and `## Task checklist` are
`code-change` only; include `## Risks / Contradictions` only when one exists.

```
# Plan: <one-sentence headline paraphrasing OBJECTIVE>

## Goal kind
<code-change | analysis | research>

## Acceptance criteria
1. <gating, outcome-based criterion>

## Verification plan
1. <gating|evidence: action + the observations that MUST be present to pass>

## Non-goals
- <out-of-scope item>

## Assumed scope
<files / modules / external deps this goal touches>

## Implementation approach
<code-change only: how to structure the code so it is easy to test>

## Task checklist
- [ ] <code-change only: first concrete implementation step>
- [ ] <next step>

## Risks / Contradictions
- <optional: an internal contradiction or infeasibility in OBJECTIVE>
```

**Acceptance criteria** ΓÇö these are the GATING set: every one must hold to pass,
so keep it SMALL (aim 3-5) and satisficing, never an exhaustive conjunction.
Numbered, concrete, one outcome each, anchored to the LITERAL objective:
do NOT invent scope. A reasonable-but-unrequested feature goes under `## Non-goals`,
never here (but a DEFINING mechanic of an artifact the OBJECTIVE names is implied
by that name ΓÇö it is requested, so it stays here) ΓÇö inflating the contract is what
makes a goal unfinishable. Each
criterion must be atomic and independently checkable from near its own start
state: never write a single holistic end-to-end gate ("drive the whole thing
through to the end"), which an automated check rarely completes ΓÇö decompose into
separate checks. Preserve OBJECTIVE's must-have terms verbatim: never swap a
named technique, technology, or artifact for an easier one; if a must-have seems
wrong or infeasible, keep it AND record the conflict under `## Risks /
Contradictions`.

**Verification plan** ΓÇö the shared procedure the implementer and the verifiers
both follow, so all judge by the SAME observable bar; cover every criterion.
Tag each step `gating` (decides pass/fail) or `evidence` (best-effort
corroboration whose absence alone, once the gating steps and honest unit checks
hold, must NOT deny completion). Each step gives the **action** (run the tests,
exercise the entry point, read the artifact) and the
**observations that MUST be** present to pass. Rules:

- Drive the REAL shipped functions/entry points from their real start state ΓÇö
  not a copy, a re-implementation, or a scenario starting past the thing checked.
- Static / structural fallback ΓÇö the BLESSED path when behavior cannot be driven
  here (a UI, a browser, a long-running interactive session): do NOT prescribe a
  flaky end-to-end run, a specific capture-file ritual, or an end-to-end outcome
  ("reach the end state") proven through test-only scaffolding. Require only the
  MINIMAL honest path: the artifact EXISTS in the source AND the shipped

- Fit every check to what is capturable in the CURRENT environment; if it cannot

- Output paths use the literal `{SCRATCH}` placeholder (e.g. `{SCRATCH}/out.log`),

the verifiers AUDIT that evidence rather than build their own. Require: real
in-repo tests that drive the shipped functions (no hardcoded expected values, no

**Assumed scope** ΓÇö specific files/modules/deps you expect to touch; do not

**Implementation approach** (`code-change` only) ΓÇö structure the work so it is
easy to test: separate pure logic from I/O and prefer small testable units.
Design guidance, NOT an acceptance criterion ΓÇö do not refute working code for
diverging from it, and do not restate it as a criterion.

**Task checklist** (`code-change` only) ΓÇö 3-8 ordered `- [ ]` checkbox steps
the implementer executes and checks off as it goes; the harness mines the first
unchecked box as the per-turn "next step" nudge. Steps are HOW guidance like
the approach, never part of the judged contract ΓÇö keep each small, concrete,
and completable in one sitting (end with a testing/evidence step). Do not put
checkboxes in any other section.

**Risks / Contradictions** (optional) ΓÇö one bullet per genuine internal
contradiction or environment infeasibility; omit when none.

# Refresh Docs

Reconcile `docs/` with the current codebase, remove documentation that no longer applies, make `docs/wiki.yaml` list every project doc that should be published to the wiki, and export the MCP-backed requirement documents.

## Preconditions

- Work from the repository root.
- Read `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` and follow its marker, plugin, session, and trust rules. Verify the marker signature and the `/health` nonce before any MCP mutation.
- Use the required MCP Server plugin for your agent (Claude/Codex/Grok) for requirements and export (`workflow.requirements.*`). Do not hand-author exported requirement docs or substitute raw REST.
- Use the operator's approved shell for all shell invocation (e.g. PowerShell.Mcp on Windows). Build YAML/JSON from native objects and serialize; never handwrite fragile payloads.
- Read facts from the code, not from memory. This skill refreshes and exports only; it does not commit or push (leave that to a wrap-up flow or an explicit request).

## Step 1 - Refresh project documentation

1. Inventory the docs surface: `docs/user/*`, `docs/architecture/*`, `docs/requirements/*.md`, `docs/testing/*`, `docs/*.md`, and `README.md` (adapt to the repo's actual layout).
2. Establish what changed since the docs were last touched: `git log --oneline` for the changed code areas, the current project/solution structure, public commands, and settings. Prefer the shipped behavior over any doc's prior claims.
3. Update each doc that drifted: renamed or removed components, changed UI/behavior, new or removed features, install commands and version pins, and cross-references. Match the existing doc voice; no em-dashes.
4. Keep the project `README.md` current as a first-class refresh target, not an afterthought: the project description and overview, the feature list, install and quickstart/usage commands, current version references, badges, and links into `docs/` must all match the shipped state. Reconcile it against the code and the refreshed docs on every run.
